prohibited_adulterants.name: Fresh Garlic
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Botulism risk from anaerobic environment. High moisture causes spoilage.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Fresh Onion
prohibited_adulterants.reason: High moisture content causes spoilage and inconsistent texture.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Fresh Herbs (General)
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Moisture promotes bacterial growth. Flavor changes unpredictably with aging.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Fresh Cilantro
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Loses all flavor during aging and develops bitter, metallic notes.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Fresh Parsley
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Turns bitter and develops metallic taste after aging.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Oil-Based Spice Pastes
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Oil suspends bacteria, creates anaerobic pockets, inhibits rind development.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Hot Sauce (Vinegar-Based)
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Vinegar weakens curds. Unpredictable pH effects. Inconsistent heat distribution.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Asafoetida (Hing)
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Overwhelmingly pungent sulfur compounds persist and intensify with aging.

prohibited_adulterants.name: Garam Masala (Blend)
prohibited_adulterants.reason: Complex blend with unpredictable aging behavior. Individual components change differently.
prohibited_adulterants.safe_alternative: Use individual spices from the blend

COLD_INFUSE.description: Steep adulterant in cold milk before heating

MILK_PREHEAT.description: Add during initial milk heating (before rennet)

CURD_MILL.description: Add while milling/stirring curds before molding
CURD_MILL.benefits: Most common stage. Even distribution. Good incorporation.
CURD_MILL.cautions: Excessive stirring may wash out flavor
suitable_for: Most herbs, spices, peppers, nuts, fruits

MOLD_LAYER.description: Layer between curds when filling molds
MOLD_LAYER.cautions: May create weak points in cheese structure

POST_PRESS.description: Apply to cheese surface after pressing
POST_PRESS.benefits: Visual appeal, concentrated flavor on exterior

BRINE_ADDITION.cautions: Some flavors don't transfer well through brine
suitable_for: Wine, beer, liquid smoke, some spices

RIND_RUB.description: Rub or wash onto rind during aging

AGING_SURFACE.description: Apply to aging cheese surface periodically

suitable_for: Fresh herbs, honey, truffle oil, delicate spices

milk_type_notes.cow: Baseline. Most adulterants work well. Mild flavor allows adulterants to shine.
milk_type_notes.goat: Tangy flavor may compete with delicate adulterants. Reduce quantities slightly. Strong spices work well.
milk_type_notes.sheep: Rich flavor and higher yield means more adulterant needed. Increase quantities 30-40%. Pairs well with bold flavors.
milk_type_notes.buffalo: High fat masks some flavors. Increase quantities 20-30%. Works well with strong spices and peppers.
milk_type_notes.camel: Unique flavor profile. Test adulterants carefully. Traditional Middle Eastern spices recommended.
milk_type_notes.yak: Rich, buttery. Similar adjustments to sheep milk.
